privacy_blockchain_intro: Most features of this application operate via Lens Protocol — a decentralized, open social protocol on the Lens Chain blockchain. This fundamentally differs from traditional centralized services and impacts how your data is stored and whether it can be deleted.
privacy_blockchain_immutable_description: Your Lens account is a smart contract (NFT) that you create and own independently via your crypto wallet. We are not the owner, operator, or custodian of this account and have no technical ability to delete, block, or modify it. Publications, subscriptions, transactions, and other actions recorded on the Lens Chain blockchain are immutable by the very nature of blockchain technology and remain there permanently, even after you stop using the application.
privacy_blockchain_offchain_description: Profile name, bio, avatar, and similar metadata are stored not directly on the blockchain, but in decentralized storage (Grove / IPFS), which the blockchain references via hash. This metadata can be updated to empty/anonymous values — which happens upon account deactivation in this app — however, prior versions of metadata at older links may technically remain accessible on the decentralized network.
privacy_blockchain_control_title: What We Control vs What We Don't
privacy_blockchain_control_description: We fully control and can permanently delete data stored on our own servers (Supabase): service logs, cache, analytics, and other data outside Lens Protocol. We do NOT control and cannot delete data recorded on the Lens Chain blockchain or in decentralized storage (Grove/IPFS/Arweave) — no application working with Lens Protocol technically possesses such capability.
privacy_nostr_identity_intro: In addition to your Lens account, the application automatically creates a second, distinct cryptographic identity for you in the Nostr protocol — a decentralized network used by this application's Native Chat feature.
privacy_nostr_identity_derivation: This identity is not randomly generated and is not stored on our servers. It is deterministically derived from your wallet signature under a fixed technical message: the same wallet always yields the same Nostr key, and it can be recreated on any device without a separate backup mechanism. The private key itself exists only in your browser memory during the session and is never sent to our servers.
privacy_nostr_identity_autolink: The public identifier of this identity (npub) is automatically written as a public metadata attribute of your Lens account on the blockchain — without a separate confirmation prompt for each action, immediately upon logging in. This happens automatically because this identity is inextricably linked to your Lens account and is intended to be publicly associated with it so other users can find you in chat. For wallets embedded via Privy, this entry occurs without extra popups; if using an external wallet (e.g. MetaMask), it may show its own signature prompt — this is an interface of the wallet itself, which the application does not control.
privacy_nostr_identity_control: Because the npub is recorded in Lens account metadata, it is subject to the same blockchain data immutability rules described above (Section 5.1): we cannot remove this record from prior metadata versions in decentralized storage, but you can clear the current value via account deactivation in settings, along with the rest of your profile metadata.
privacy_storage_content: Content you publish via Lens Protocol (posts, comments, reactions) enters the blockchain and/or decentralized storage and is stored indefinitely, regardless of this app's actions. Data stored exclusively on our own servers is retained while the account is active or according to periods required for stated processing purposes.
privacy_deletion_account: 'Account Deactivation' in app settings means: (1) disconnecting the app session from your Lens account; (2) clearing public profile metadata (name, bio, avatar) to empty values; (3) complete deletion of all data about you from our own servers; (4) clearing app local data on your device. This does NOT delete the blockchain account itself, transaction history, or already published entries on Lens Chain — this is technically impossible, as described in 'Blockchain Data' above.
privacy_sharing_supabase: Storage of off-chain data: the moderation queue, notifications, help requests, and action rate-limiting. Servers located in the US/EU (with a DPA)
privacy_sharing_hosting_description: Frontend hosting, CDN, and CAPTCHA verification (Cloudflare Turnstile) during registration and other sensitive actions
privacy_no_selling: We do NOT sell your data.
privacy_right_deletion: Erasure ('right to be forgotten') — applies to data we actually control; does not extend to immutable blockchain records (see 'Blockchain Data')
privacy_transfers_description: Data may be transferred to the US and other countries outside the EU.

terms_lens_nature: Nature of Lens Account and Blockchain Data
terms_lens_nature_description: The account you create via Lens Protocol is a smart contract (NFT) on the Lens Chain blockchain, which you exclusively own via your crypto wallet. The Platform is not the owner, custodian, or administrator of this account and lacks technical capability to delete it or modify data already recorded on the blockchain, as blockchain records are immutable by nature. Account deactivation in this app revokes access and removes Platform-controlled data, but does not delete the blockchain account or published records. For details, see 'Blockchain Data' in Privacy Policy.

welcome_to_hrp_dao: Welcome to Dossier by Human Rights Policy Decentralized Autonomous Organization
about_subtitle: Dossier — a Human Rights Policy DAO project
about_intro: a decentralized platform for recording, publishing, and discussing human rights violations, created and governed by the community rather than a single company or government.
about_mission_description: We believe information about human rights violations should remain immutable, verifiable, and outside the control of any single party. Dossier empowers people to document events, request aid, and bring violations to public oversight on infrastructure that no one can quietly delete or edit.
about_feature_reports: Publishing and viewing reports of human rights violations linked to location and severity level
about_feature_map: An interactive map to explore violations and country ratings worldwide
about_feature_help_requests: A help request board so people in distress can be found and supported by the community
about_feature_governance: Community governance for reviewing reports, resolving disputes, and moderating content
about_decentralized_description: Posts and profiles exist on Lens Protocol network, so content is not owned by a single server or company. Part of the project's logic — including content moderation and sanctions — is recorded on-chain, making the process verifiable by anyone rather than relying on trust in an anonymous back-office.
about_dao_description: Human Rights Policy DAO is a decentralized autonomous organization: rules, moderation decisions, and policy updates are proposed and voted on through on-chain governance rather than an individual owner. Anyone with appropriate governance rights can participate in shaping how the platform works.
about_independence_description: Dossier is a community-run technical platform. It is not a government agency, law enforcement institution, or substitute for legal or humanitarian services — for full details on what the platform is and is not, see the Terms of Service.
about_contact_description: Questions, feedback, or collaboration proposals can be sent via the in-app support page or through DAO governance and community channels.
privacy_sharing_gemini_description: Processing messages you send to the Atticus AI advisor (see the dedicated section below)
privacy_cross_app_description: Dossier and the DAO governance app share the same authentication system (Privy), so one wallet/account works in both apps. Moderation and sanctions against accounts that break the rules are not decided here, but in a separate DAO app through a public community vote. When you follow a link from one app to the other (e.g. from the "Governance" section), your wallet address may be passed as a URL parameter so the other app recognizes you immediately without reconnecting.
privacy_ai_description: If you use the built-in Atticus AI advisor, the text of your messages and the current conversation history are sent to a third-party provider — the Google Gemini API — to generate a reply. We do not retain your conversations with Atticus on our own servers any longer than needed to produce that reply; conversation history is kept only in your browser's memory for the duration of the session. Atticus's responses are for informational purposes only and are not legal advice — see the corresponding disclaimer in the Terms of Service.
privacy_tips_description: The "Support the author" feature lets you send other users tips in test tokens (tUSD/tGHO) on the Lens Chain test network — these tokens currently have no real monetary value and are minted for free via a built-in "mint" function on the test page. These transactions happen directly wallet-to-wallet on the blockchain and are publicly visible there; the Platform is not a party to these transactions, does not process payment cards, and does not hold funds.
terms_dao_moderation_title: Complaint Review and Sanctions via the DAO
terms_dao_moderation_description: Beyond the Platform's right to promptly hide content that clearly violates these Terms (Sec. 5.1), ongoing sanctions against an account (restriction, ban) are not decided unilaterally — they go through a separate DAO governance app: anyone can file a complaint, which becomes a public proposal, is discussed on the forum, and is put to a community vote. The outcome is executed on-chain, automatically. Both apps — Dossier and the DAO — share the same wallet/account (via Privy), so actions taken against your account in the DAO app affect your profile here as well.
terms_ai_disclaimer_title: Atticus AI Advisor — Not Legal Advice
terms_ai_disclaimer_description: The built-in Atticus AI advisor provides general, informational content based on constitutional and international human rights law. It is an automated system, not a lawyer, government body, or human rights organization; its responses may contain errors, inaccuracies, or outdated information. Do not rely on Atticus's responses as final legal advice for your specific situation — consult a qualified lawyer or relevant organization instead. Messages you send to Atticus are processed by a third-party provider (Google Gemini API) — see the Privacy Policy for details.
terms_tips_description: The "Support the author" feature lets you send other users tips directly, wallet-to-wallet, on the blockchain. These are currently test tokens (tUSD/tGHO) on the Lens Chain test network, minted for free with no real monetary value; should this change, this clause will be updated. The Platform is not a party to these transactions, does not process payment cards, does not hold funds in custody, and does not refund tips sent — all blockchain transactions are final and irreversible.
terms_chat_description: Native chat messages are transmitted over the decentralized Nostr network rather than the Platform's own servers, so our ability to delete or moderate messages already sent is limited — they may remain available on relay servers outside the Platform's control. The same content prohibitions that apply to public content (Section 2) apply to chat messages. We are not responsible for the content of messages sent by other users through this channel.
